title: Constructible comparison
statement:
For Noetherian $\Lambda$, a sheaf on $X_{\Proet}$ is constructible if locally on $X$
a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata makes it locally
constant of finite type on each stratum.

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For a discrete Noetherian
$\Lambda$, every constructible pro-étale $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf is classical.
The functor $\nu_X^*$ gives an equivalence from constructible étale sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules to $\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$, and an equivalence
$D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ of bounded constructible derived
categories.

proof.text: Use classicality in the precise sense of [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map]: for every pro-etale affine presentation $U\cong\varprojlim_{i\in I}U_i$ indexed by a small cofiltered category in the fixed site universes, the continuity map $\varinjlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U_i)\to F(U)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules. The scalar action on sections comes from $\Lambda\to\Lambda_X(V)$. On a general $X$ use these inverse-limit presentations; the identification with affine ind-etale objects is only used over an affine base. For discrete $\Lambda$, the finite constant local models in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] are constant sheaves of finitely presented $\Lambda$-modules, using the coefficient identification $\Lambda_X=\nu_X^*\Lambda_{X,\Et}$ in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Over the Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, finite-type models are finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]; a finite presentation conversely supplies finitely many generators. Thus the local finite-partition condition in the first paragraph is exactly the affine-local constructibility condition, with no Noetherian hypothesis on $X$. On qcqs $X$ this also yields the finite global stratification required by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: choose a finite affine open cover $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ with finite partitions $V_j=\coprod_k Z_{jk}$ carrying these models. Each $V_j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. For a quasi-compact open $W\subset X$, the affine basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and quasi-compactness give a finite affine open covering $W=\bigcup_l W_l$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], every $V_j\cap W_l$ is quasi-compact; their finite union $V_j\cap W$ is quasi-compact. Thus $V_j$ is retrocompact. If $A\subset V_j$ is open and retrocompact in $V_j$, then $A\cap W=A\cap(V_j\cap W)$ is quasi-compact, so $A$ is also retrocompact in $X$. The finite-difference definition in [def-weil-constructible-subset] therefore makes each $Z_{jk}$ constructible in $X$. Set $T_{jk}=Z_{jk}\setminus\bigcup_{h<j}V_h$. These finitely many pieces are constructible by the Boolean-algebra clause of that definition, locally closed because each is a locally closed $Z_{jk}$ intersected with a closed subset, pairwise disjoint, and cover $X$. Pulling back each local constant trivialization to $T_{jk}$ retains its finitely presented model, so this is the required global stratification. Conversely, intersecting a finite global stratification with an affine open retains locally closed constructible pieces: an open retrocompact $A\subset X$ restricts to a retrocompact open there because every quasi-compact open of that affine open is also a quasi-compact open of $X$. The displayed constant models restrict as well. For qcqs $X$, apply [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical], including its final locally stratified clause, to conclude that every constructible $F$ is classical. The empty scheme and zero sheaf are included.

proof.text:
Use the affine-local definition of constructible etale modules in [def-pe-etale-constructible-module]; the coefficient ring is Noetherian, and the constant models need only be finitely generated as modules. Let $G$ be an etale constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf. On each constructible locally closed stratum $i:Z	o X$ of a local stratification, the first, underived inverse-image clause of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], used in the inverse direction, identifies $i^*
u_X^*G$ with $
u_Z^*i^*G$. The models of $i^*G$ are finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], so [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] shows that this restriction is a pro-etale local system with the same finite-presentation models. Hence $
u_X^*G$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The functor is fully faithful on all module sheaves by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Conversely let $F$ be constructible. By [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical] and [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], put $G=
u_{X,*}F$ and obtain $
u_X^*G\cong F$. For each stratum $i:Z	o X$ on which $i^*F$ is locally constant of finite type, its models are finitely presented by the same algebra lemma, and [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] supplies an etale local system $H$ of finitely presented modules with $
u_Z^*H\cong i^*F$. Pullback compatibility gives $
u_Z^*i^*G\cong
u_Z^*H$. Full faithfulness on $Z$ lifts this isomorphism and its inverse uniquely; their composites lift the identity, so $i^*G\cong H$. The very same local strata therefore make $G$ etale constructible. This proves essential surjectivity and the constructible sheaf equivalence, without any separate gluing assertion.

proof.text:
Classicality for complexes means classicality of every cohomology sheaf, with the same presentation and module conventions, by clause 4 of [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map]. Here $D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ has the bounded constructible-cohomology meaning of [def-pe-etale-constructible-module]. By [sk-prop-sf-comparison], the bounded-below derived unit is an isomorphism for our discrete Noetherian $\Lambda$; this verifies the hypothesis of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence]. We may therefore use its inverse equivalences on $D^+$ and the subcategory with classical cohomology. Exactness of $
u_X^*$ from [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] gives $H^q(
u_X^*L)\cong
u_X^*H^q(L)$: applying an exact functor preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology. For $L\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, step 2 makes these sheaves constructible and they vanish outside the finite cohomological interval of $L$, so its pullback belongs to $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ as defined in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Conversely, for $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$, its cohomology sheaves are classical by [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical]. The derived equivalence supplies $L=R
u_{X,*}K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with $
u_X^*L\cong K$. Thus $
u_X^*H^q(L)\cong H^q(K)$. Step 2 and full faithfulness identify $H^q(L)$ with the constructible etale antecedent $
u_{X,*}H^q(K)$. If $H^q(K)=0$, faithfulness forces $1_{H^q(L)}=0$, so $H^q(L)=0$. Consequently $L$ is bounded in the same finite interval and lies in $D^b_c$. Restricting the fully faithful derived equivalence to these full subcategories proves the claimed bounded constructible equivalence.
